requirements.summary: Scoped to integration failures where the host-selected browser port differs from container defaults or fails to propagate through settings, launchers, and packaged runtime support.

Compared Compose/Docker health probing, settings persistence, both offline launcher paths, and release packager contents.

design.summary: Keep container service port fixed at 8080; derive browser-origin settings from the active page; bind WebAuthn ceremonies to the validated request origin; reconcile persisted host-port changes in each offline launcher without removing shared volumes.
evidence: Unix bundle already had fallback selection and a host-side port watcher; Windows bundle was brought to the same lifecycle.
Launcher child script paths are explicitly quoted so packages installed under paths containing spaces can start their agents.

implementation.summary: Fixed four confirmed integration defects: WebAuthn origin/port mismatch, stale settings-page port display, missing Windows offline fallback/watcher, and Windows child-script path quoting.
evidence: WebAuthn start validates localhost Origin and binds it to the one-use challenge; finish requires the same origin.
Accessibility host-port control renders the active browser port including implicit 80/443.
Windows offline startup chooses and persists a free fallback; Windows and combined full packages include watch-port.ps1 to reconcile saved port through Compose.
Windows launcher quotes update-agent.ps1 and watch-port.ps1 paths passed to Start-Process.
